issue: Web-searched for revival at the Antifer site (cancelled 2013, prior sponsor Gaz de Normandie SAS / Poweo-CIM). No revival by the original sponsor: the 2011-era Gaz de Normandie coverage confirming the project 'maintained pending the next GPMH call for proposals' predates the 2013 cancellation and is not evidence of any 2025-2026 activity -- no subsequent Gaz de Normandie announcement was found. However, found a DIFFERENT, much earlier-stage signal: GRTgaz's March 2023 ten-year transmission development plan discloses 'opportunity studies' for three possible new Le Havre-area import projects (two onshore terminals + one floating unit), with the floating option potentially moored at the port of Antifer in Saint-Jouin-Bruneval -- the same physical site as the cancelled GEM record. This is a network-operator capacity study, not a sponsored project: no developer/operator identified, no site confirmed (the mayor of Saint-Jouin-Bruneval said he had never been informed), no permit or regulatory filing. Well below the sponsor+location+concrete-step threshold, so NOT staged as new_terminal; staged as monitor_list (see france.monitor.json) given it names the same historically-dormant site and could mature into a real dead-and-revived case in a future batch.
suggested_action: No edit to T100000130454 (stays cancelled). Track the GRTgaz opportunity-study signal via the monitor_list entry.

issue: Web-searched for revival at the Fos-sur-Mer / Fos Faster site (cancelled 2014-2015, sponsor Fos Faster LNG Terminal SAS). No revival evidence found for 2025-2026: the project owner formally told the CNDP (national public-debate commission) in Dec 2015 the LNG terminal project was abandoned, and no subsequent LNG-specific announcement at this site was found. The only current Fos-sur-Mer LNG-adjacent activity is Elengy's separate 'Medhyterra' project -- a LOW-CARBON AMMONIA import terminal (30,000 m3 tank replacing a decommissioned LNG tank, FID expected 2026, commissioning 2029) sited at the existing, still-operating Fos Tonkin LNG Terminal (T100000130452), which already carries a 'proposed / Ammonia Import Terminal' unit row in the current GEM export -- i.e. this is already captured, not a gap, and ammonia (NH3) is an out-of-scope/read-only field per methodology regardless.
suggested_action: No action needed. Terminal stays cancelled; the Medhyterra ammonia unit is already represented on Fos Tonkin and NH3 fields are read-only.
